summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted due to concern for recurrent lower extremity cellulitis, following a primary care visit where her legs appeared more swollen and weepy. Although physical findings were not classic for acute infection, given her history of recurrent cellulitis and prior response to IV vancomycin, a PICC line was placed and treatment with IV vancomycin was initiated for a 7-day course. She also had symptoms of volume overload from chronic diastolic heart failure, for which she received IV furosemide and was restarted on oral Bumetanide. Her phenytoin level was therapeutic, and her INR was subtherapeutic at 1.3, requiring outpatient monitoring. She improved clinically and was discharged home with plans for home IV antibiotics, weight monitoring, and follow-up for INR and infectious disease evaluation.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of other female genital organs
